## Discoveries 458–460 — smooth Tanaka limits and a positive monotone L2 residual

The preceding discovery456–457 constructed the actual sign integrand and its stochastic integral. This turn continued that active proof route rather than ingesting another manuscript. The specific question was whether the existing native Ito and operator machinery can construct any of the missing Brownian local-time foundation, instead of accepting local time as an input. Rechecked the current sign module and the native C2/smooth Ito, bounded approximation and L2 dominated-convergence interfaces before editing. Source context remains the user's genuine sticky-flow question and the previously audited sticky manuscripts, preserved under their existing hashes; no manuscript theorem or proof was used as an assumption.

### 458 — explicit smooth convex absolute-value approximations

`Foundation/SmoothAbsoluteApproximation.lean` constructs, for an actual positive real parameter e,

f_e(x)=sqrt(x^2+e^2),

f'_e(x)=x/sqrt(x^2+e^2),

f''_e(x)=e^2/(sqrt(x^2+e^2))^3.

The first and second formulas are proved to equal the actual Mathlib derivatives by ordinary differentiation. Native results establish smoothness at every order, |x|<=f_e(x)<=|x|+e, uniform error at most e, |f'_e|<=1, nonnegative curvature and |f''_e|<=1/e. Thus f_e is 1-Lipschitz and its actual derivative is 1/e-Lipschitz. No arbitrary derivative candidate is supplied to Ito.

### 459 — pass actual Brownian terminal values and coefficient fields to their limits

`Foundation/BrownianTanakaApproximation.lean` uses the explicit positive sequence e_n=1/(n+1). It proves pointwise convergence of the smooth slopes to the measurable sign function, including x=0. A reusable joint representative theorem identifies the existing predictable Lipschitz field with the finite-horizon indicator times its scalar function of the actual continuous Brownian source.

The slope fields are dominated in absolute value by the already constructed sign field. Native L2 dominated convergence therefore gives convergence in the actual time/probability L2 space, and hence in the raw predictable domain, to sign(B_t) on (0,T]. Continuity of the verified stochastic integral gives

integral_0^T f'_(e_n)(B_t) dB_t -> N_T in L2.

The terminal uniform-error bound independently gives f_(e_n)(B_T) -> |B_T| in Gaussian L2. The limiting absolute-value class is identified almost everywhere with |clockPath(T)|. The global Lipschitz function itself is not assumed bounded; the argument uses its actual uniform approximation error on the probability space.

### 460 — a positive, monotone, L2-continuous residual

`Foundation/BrownianTanakaResidual.lean` independently defines the actual smooth curvature drifts as Gaussian-L2 Bochner integrals

A_n(T)=(1/2) integral_0^T f''_(e_n)(B_t) dt.

The existing C2 Ito theorem, instantiated with the proved actual derivatives and bounds, proves

A_n(T)=f_(e_n)(B_T)-e_n-integral_0^T f'_(e_n)(B_t) dB_t.

The deterministic initial value is e_n, so no initial-value term is silently discarded. The drift curves are genuinely integrable; their continuity is inherited from the existing bounded-curvature construction. The usual order on L2 is identified with almost-everywhere scalar order, and positive scalar multiplication is proved to preserve it locally. Bochner integration of the nonnegative curvature gives A_n(T)>=0. Positivity of the intervening interval integral also gives A_n(S)<=A_n(T) for S<=T.

Define L_T=|B_T|-N_T as an actual Gaussian L2 class. The preceding terminal and stochastic limits prove A_n(T)->L_T in L2. Closedness of the positive cone then proves L_T>=0, and closedness of the order relation proves L_S<=L_T for S<=T. Native theorems additionally prove L_0=0 and continuity of T->L_T in L2. The sign-integral L2 continuity is derived from its exact verified covariance, rather than postulated.

The displayed fixed-time identity |B_T|=N_T+L_T is algebraic from the residual definition; the mathematical construction content is its identification as the limit of independently defined curvature drifts and the proved positivity/monotonicity/continuity properties. The Gaussian sample space does not imply that every random variable in its L2 space is Gaussian. No Brownian-law assertion for N is being inferred from its covariance alone.

### What this establishes and what remains

This is a positive construction of a candidate local-time family in the actual L2 space. The monotonicity theorem is order on equivalence classes: for each fixed S<=T, the inequality holds almost surely. The continuity theorem is continuity into L2. Neither statement by itself supplies one jointly measurable version with continuous increasing sample paths for every time on a single probability-one event. In particular, L2 continuity plus monotonicity does not generally imply continuous sample paths.

A productive next construction is to realize the smooth drift approximants pathwise, identify their sections with these Bochner classes, and establish enough uniform-in-time control to construct a continuous limiting version. The support of its Stieltjes mass on Brownian zeros, occupation identities and the normalization required by a sticky clock still need proofs. A smooth Ito formula and a limit identity are not substitutes for those assertions.

The earlier zero-density obstruction454–455 remains intact: a singular local-time forward clock in the original Brownian parameter cannot be replaced by a Lebesgue density supported on Brownian zeros. The new positive L2 family does not instantiate the deterministic inverse clock424 yet, because that clock needs an actual continuous nonnegative path with proved hypotheses. Adaptedness and measurability of the random inverse, strong Markov/sticky generator identification, the speed/reference measure, compatible multi-point motions and a genuine stochastic kernel flow remain unresolved.

## Discoveries 461–462 — actual smooth mass paths and their stochastic realization

Continued the productive Tanaka construction after458–460. The new question was whether the independently constructed L2 curvature drifts are represented by actual continuous increasing random paths. This is needed before any limiting path or sticky clock can be constructed; merely knowing positivity and continuity into L2 is insufficient. Rechecked the current residual, Brownian path source and native representative-Fubini machinery. No new manuscript proof or bulk intake occurred. Source context remains the user's sticky-flow foundation question and the prior preserved sticky sources; the new arguments use proved library theorems, not manuscript assumptions.

### 461 — construct measurable continuous increasing smooth mass paths

`Foundation/BrownianSmoothMassPath.lean` constructs, for e_n=1/(n+1),

A_n(omega,T)=(1/2) integral_0^T e_n^2/(B_s(omega)^2+e_n^2)^(3/2) ds.

The implementation uses the positive square-root radius cubed, exactly the curvature proved458. Its time integrand is continuous along the already constructed actual Brownian continuous path and jointly measurable in time and sample. Ordinary FTC proves the primitive's actual derivative and continuity. Nonnegative curvature and adjacent-interval integration prove monotonicity. Restricting to nonnegative time yields an actual continuous-map-valued random variable with A_n(omega,0)=0 and A_n(omega,T)>=0.

These smooth path properties hold for every sample in the existing path construction, not only after an uncountable almost-everywhere quantifier interchange. A separate argument proves each coordinate is measurable by measurable parameter integration; the continuous-path Borel criterion then proves measurability into C(nonnegative reals,reals). Joint measurability of the resulting process follows from coordinate measurability and path continuity.

### 462 — identify the paths with the actual Bochner drifts

`Foundation/BrownianSmoothMassRealization.lean` proves that the native Gaussian curvature-value class has the actual continuous Brownian curvature as a representative at every fixed time. It then applies the existing representative-Fubini theorem on each finite horizon: the L2-valued section curve is genuinely integrable, the scalar joint kernel is measurable and its sections are identified almost everywhere. This justifies, rather than assumes, interchange of scalar representatives and the Gaussian-L2 Bochner integral.

Consequently the pathwise A_n(omega,T) agrees almost surely with the independently constructed `approximateMass n T`. Its fixed-time coordinate is square-integrable. The native L2 class of that coordinate is exactly the previous Bochner class, and these actual path-coordinate classes converge in L2 to the verified positive monotone residual L_T from460.

The module also constructs measurable continuous compensated paths

M_n(omega,T)=sqrt(B_T(omega)^2+e_n^2)-e_n-A_n(omega,T).

The actual smooth Ito identity and the new representative theorem prove that their fixed-time coordinates agree almost surely with the completed stochastic integral of f'_(e_n)(B_s). The native conditional Ito theorem, including the proved horizon-cutoff identity, yields the actual conditional-expectation relation E[M_n(T)|raw Brownian past at S]=M_n(S) almost surely for fixed S<=T.

The raw-adaptation scope remains precise: the continuous modification is identified with raw-past L2 classes at each fixed time. No pointwise raw strong-adaptation assertion or Mathlib Martingale predicate for these chosen continuous representatives is inferred solely from those equivalences. No terminal Gaussian law is inferred merely because the ambient probability space is Gaussian.

A productive next step is a maximal or uniform-in-time estimate for differences of the compensated martingale approximants, using the actual conditional identities and existing integral isometry. Any use of finite-time martingale inequalities must verify the required adaptation and measurable-version hypotheses, rather than silently transferring pointwise raw measurability through almost-sure equality.

Support of limiting mass on Brownian zeros, the occupation/local-time identity and clock normalization remain unproved. ## Discoveries 463–464 — adapted envelopes and a finite-grid maximal estimate

Continued the actual Tanaka-path construction after461–462. The immediate obstacle was that fixed-time L2 convergence alone does not construct a uniform continuous path limit. Rechecked the current compensated-path representatives, raw-past conditional Ito theorem, and the pinned Mathlib conditional Jensen and discrete maximal-inequality interfaces. No new manuscript proof or bulk intake occurred. Source context remains the user's sticky-flow foundation question and the preserved sticky manuscripts; all new arguments are independent native proofs.

### 463 — construct an adapted nonnegative conditional envelope

`Foundation/ConditionalEnvelopeMaximal.lean` works on an arbitrary finite measure space with a discrete filtration. For a genuinely integrable terminal real function F, construct

E_i=max(E[|F||filtration_i],0).

The conditional-expectation process is an actual raw strongly adapted martingale. Its pointwise maximum with zero is an actual submartingale, nonnegative at every sample, satisfying the hypotheses of the pinned Mathlib `MeasureTheory.maximal_ineq` theorem. Conditional Jensen gives |E[F|filtration_i]|<=E_i almost surely. A separate theorem identifies E_i almost surely with the unmodified conditional expectation of |F|, so its integral is the actual terminal L1 norm.

Mathlib's discrete maximal inequality and positivity of the terminal envelope yield the verified bound

epsilon * measure{some i<=N has f_i>=epsilon} <= integral |F|

whenever each f_i is dominated almost surely by E_i. The countable conjunction of these domination events is justified explicitly before comparing the finite crossing events. The positive-part construction avoids pretending that an arbitrary almost-surely nonnegative representative is pointwise nonnegative. No adaptation of a chosen continuous modification is assumed merely from fixed-time almost-sure equality.

### 464 — specialize to the actual smooth compensated Brownian paths

`Foundation/BrownianSmoothGridMaximal.lean` constructs the discrete raw Brownian filtration at a monotone bounded sequence of times tau_i<=T. Its terminal function is the actual Gaussian-L2 class

F=M_n(T)-M_m(T),

where these M terms are the already constructed completed Ito integrals. The verified conditional Ito and horizon-cutoff formulas identify E[F|raw past at tau_i] with the difference of the actual continuous compensated paths at tau_i, almost surely. Thus their absolute differences are dominated by the constructed adapted envelope, with every required finite-measure, integrability and filtration hypothesis discharged.

A native Gaussian probability-space Cauchy–Schwarz argument proves integral|F|<=||F||_2. The actual integral isometry proves

||F||_2=||approximateField(n,T)-approximateField(m,T)||_2.

The resulting native finite-grid maximal probability estimate is

epsilon * P{there exists i<=N with |M_n(tau_i)-M_m(tau_i)|>=epsilon}
  <= ||approximateField(n,T)-approximateField(m,T)||_2.

The formal inequality uses nonnegative extended-real probability values and an ofReal conversion of the finite norm, so epsilon=0 is also covered without division by zero. It holds for every finite prefix of every monotone time sequence bounded by T. The right-hand side is independent of the grid size; the field sequence converges in the actual predictable L2 space by459. A weak L1 maximal bound is sufficient for a potential uniform-convergence-in-probability route; an L2 maximal inequality has not been asserted or needed for this result.

### Why the scope is still finite-grid

The theorem controls the actual already constructed continuous paths at a finite time grid. It does not yet prove a bound over every time in [0,T], nor construct a limiting continuous random path. One bounded monotone infinite time sequence is not itself a dense enumeration of the whole interval. Passing to all times requires a justified family of finite increasingly fine grids, continuity, measurable crossing events and probability limits. A fast subsequence and uniform-limit construction would then still be needed to obtain an actual continuous limiting version.

For the mass paths, the uniform scalar approximation bounds from458 must also be connected to differences of their compensated paths. No unproved uniform-in-time convergence of the curvature drifts is silently substituted for the established fixed-time L2 convergence. Support of limiting mass on Brownian zeros, occupation identities, normalization and a genuine sticky diffusion/compatible multi-point kernel flow remain unconstructed. The deterministic inverse-clock constructor and abstract operator/semigroup machinery still cannot supply those stochastic existence hypotheses by themselves.

## Discoveries 465–467 — compact-time maximal control and uniform Cauchy estimates

Continued the productive Tanaka proof after the finite-grid bound463–464. Rechecked that bound and the actual continuous compensated-path representatives before passing to compact time. No new manuscript proof or bulk document intake occurred. The mathematical question remains the user's genuine sticky-flow foundation question; the following constructions use verified library objects and do not assume a manuscript's stochastic realization.

### 465 — arbitrary finite and countable time sets

`Foundation/BrownianSmoothFiniteSetMaximal.lean` removes the monotone-grid restriction from the finite event. A finite subset of [0,T] is sorted using its actual order embedding from Fin(cardinality), then extended constantly to a bounded monotone natural-time sequence. Every member of the finite set occurs in the controlled prefix, with no multiplicity or cardinality factor in the estimate. The empty set is handled separately.

For an arbitrary countable collection u_i<=T, the proof controls its finite prefixes and identifies their increasing union with the countable crossing event. Continuity of measure from below and multiplication through the extended-real supremum retain the same bound. This avoids the invalid shortcut of treating a single monotone bounded infinite sequence as a dense enumeration of an interval.

### 466 — the whole compact interval

`Foundation/BrownianSmoothCompactMaximal.lean` constructs a dense natural sequence in the nonempty separable subtype {t>=0:t<=T}. Every continuous compensated path difference that strictly exceeds epsilon at some time also strictly exceeds epsilon at a dense sample time. The converse is immediate from membership of the sample time in the interval. This proves an exact countable representation of the strict whole-interval crossing event and its measurability from the already proved coordinate measurability.

The countable maximal bound then gives the native compact-time estimate

epsilon * P{there exists t<=T with |M_n(t)-M_m(t)|>epsilon}
  <= ||approximateField(n,T)-approximateField(m,T)||_2.

The crossing event is strict: continuity and density do not automatically detect an isolated equality with a non-strict threshold. The implementation respects that distinction. The probability is evaluated on the actual continuous compensated paths, rather than on hypothetical path representatives of the abstract L2 limit.

### 467 — uniformly Cauchy in probability, including the mass paths

`Foundation/BrownianSmoothUniformCauchy.lean` proves the normalized uniform scalar estimate

|sqrt(x^2+e_n^2)-e_n-|x||<=e_n.

The actual path definitions then yield, for every sample and time,

|A_n(t)-A_m(t)|<=e_n+e_m+|M_n(t)-M_m(t)|.

This deterministic comparison also gives a compact-time maximal bound for mass-path crossings above epsilon+e_n+e_m. No uniform convergence of the curvature densities is assumed; they can concentrate as n grows.

Since the actual predictable coefficient sequence converges in L2, it is Cauchy. For positive epsilon and delta, its terminal norm difference is eventually less than epsilon*delta. Applying the compact estimate and cancelling the finite positive epsilon in extended-real arithmetic proves

there exists N such that for all n,m>=N,
P{some t<=T has |M_n(t)-M_m(t)|>epsilon}<delta.

Using the deterministic mass comparison, the same native epsilon–delta statement is proved for A_n-A_m. The proof uses the compensated estimate at epsilon/2 and e_n,e_m<epsilon/4. Both are uniform-in-time Cauchy estimates for the actual constructed paths, not merely fixed-time convergence statements.

This closes the finite-grid-to-compact-time gap and supplies the probability control needed for a fast-subsequence argument. Those are the next actual existence steps; the Cauchy estimates alone are not reported as a completed path construction.

Positivity, monotonicity and the zero initial value could then be inherited from the existing smooth mass paths after a justified uniform limit. ## Discoveries 468–470 — an actual measurable continuous Tanaka-residual path

Continued the productive local-time construction after the compact-time Cauchy estimates465–467. The next question was whether those estimates actually yield a continuous random path, rather than just an abstract Cauchy family. Rechecked the current probability bounds, native Borel–Cantelli, compact continuous-map completeness, compact-open uniformity and measurable-version interfaces. No new manuscript proof or bulk intake occurred. Source context remains the user's genuine sticky-flow question and the prior preserved sticky manuscripts; no manuscript result is assumed.

### 468 — choose a fast increasing subsequence and prove one good event

`Foundation/BrownianMassFastSubsequence.lean` uses tolerance eta_j=2^(-j) and horizon j+1. The actual uniform-Cauchy theorem supplies a cutoff for every stage, with crossing probability below eta_j whenever both indices exceed that cutoff. A recursively defined subsequence takes the maximum of the next cutoff and the previous index plus1. Native theorems prove that it is strictly increasing and meets every corresponding cutoff.

The bad event at stage j is that the successive selected mass paths differ by more than eta_j somewhere before time j+1. Its probability is bounded by eta_j. The geometric series is summable, so native Borel–Cantelli proves a single probability-one event on which eventually, for every time t<=j+1, the successive selected paths differ by at most eta_j. The time quantifier is inside the good event; no invalid uncountable intersection of fixed-time almost-sure statements is used.

### 469 — compact-uniform convergence and a measurable continuous path limit

`Foundation/BrownianMassContinuousLimit.lean` first restricts selected paths to each compact interval [0,T]. On a good sample, shift the sequence past both the random exceptional initial segment and a deterministic integer beyond T. The compact supremum distance between successive shifted paths is bounded by a geometric sequence. The verified geometric Cauchy theorem proves Cauchyness in the complete space of continuous functions on [0,T]; a shift does not affect Cauchyness.

The compact-open uniformity basis then proves that the selected entire paths are Cauchy in C(nonnegative reals,reals). Every compact time set is bounded by a finite T, so the preceding restrictions control every basic entourage. Completeness of the continuous-map space supplies an actual continuous limit path on each good sample. The preliminary choice is zero off the good event, and convergence of the measurable path sequence proves its almost-everywhere measurability. The standard measurable-version construction then yields an actual measurable map into the continuous-path space.

Native theorems prove that, almost surely, the selected mass paths converge to this map in compact-open topology, hence uniformly on every finite horizon simultaneously. On one probability-one event, the limit starts at zero, is monotone and is nonnegative for every time. These properties follow from the actual path convergence and the properties of the already constructed smooth paths, not from hypotheses supplied to a new stochastic object. The measurable-version replacement preserves the statements almost surely; it does not assert every bad sample has those order properties.

### 470 — identify the path with the independently proved residual

`Foundation/BrownianMassLimitIdentification.lean` compares two actual limits at each fixed time T. The selected drift classes converge in Gaussian L2 to L_T=|B_T|-N_T by460. L2 convergence gives convergence in measure and a further almost-sure subsequence. The path-space convergence from469 gives coordinate convergence along that same further subsequence. Uniqueness of scalar limits and the previously proved representative-Fubini identities identify the actual limit coordinate with the original residual class almost surely.

Thus every fixed-time coordinate is genuinely square-integrable and its native L2 class equals L_T. The actual random path is jointly measurable in time and sample. Its fixed-time coordinate has a raw-past almost-everywhere strongly measurable representative, because it agrees with the verified raw-past residual class. No pointwise raw strong-adaptation assertion for the chosen continuous representative is inferred merely from almost-sure equality.

The native fixed-time Tanaka identity is now

|clockPath(omega,T)|=N_T(omega)+limitPath(omega,T) almost surely.

Here N_T is the actual previously constructed sign Ito-integral class, and limitPath is the actual measurable continuous random path just constructed. Identification is proved by independently convergent limits. This is stronger than defining an arbitrary residual class and labeling it local time, and it closes the previously recorded continuous-path existence gap. The displayed identity is still a fixed-T equality with a chosen representative of N_T; it is not reported as a simultaneous all-time identity for the arbitrary original Ito representatives.

### The remaining stochastic-realization boundary

There is now an actual measurable continuous increasing Tanaka-residual path, with order/zero properties on one good event and fixed-time L2 identification. Support of its Stieltjes mass on Brownian zeros, an occupation/local-time identity and the normalization needed for a declared sticky model remain separate unproved assertions. A useful next pathwise question is whether the uniform approximants show that limiting mass is constant on compact intervals where the Brownian path stays uniformly away from zero. That would begin the support proof using actual curvature concentration, rather than assuming it.

The deterministic inverse-clock result424 can only contribute to a genuine sticky realization once its stochastic input is correctly identified and the random inverse's measurability/adaptedness and strong Markov/generator properties are established. A continuous increasing residual alone does not establish sticky speed measure, compatible multi-point motions or a stochastic kernel flow. No genuine sticky flow, NS/YM equivalence, continuum gap or Millennium result is asserted.

## Discoveries 471–474 — nontrivial atomless mass supported on Brownian zeros

Continued the productive pathwise Tanaka construction after the actual continuous limit468–470. The next independent mathematical question was whether this increasing residual really stays constant away from Brownian zeros, and whether the resulting zero-supported mass can be proved nontrivial. Rechecked the existing actual curvature, continuous path limit, Gaussian observation law and native Stieltjes/support interfaces. No new manuscript proof or bulk intake occurred. Source context remains the user's sticky stochastic-flow question and the prior preserved sticky manuscripts; no claimed manuscript theorem is used as a hypothesis.

### 471 — quantitative curvature concentration

`Foundation/BrownianCurvatureConcentration.lean` proves from the actual curvature formula that, for e>0 and delta>0,

delta<=|x| implies f''_e(x)<=e^2/delta^3.

The denominator estimate uses sqrt(x^2+e^2)>=|x|. Ordinary adjacent-interval integration identifies increments of the actual smooth mass paths with half the curvature integral on that interval. If a Brownian path stays at least delta away from zero on [s,t], then

0<=A_n(t)-A_n(s)<=(1/2)(t-s)e_n^2/delta^3.

Every term is from an independently constructed actual path integral. No support or occupation assertion is supplied to this estimate.

### 472 — no increase on zero-free compact intervals

`Foundation/BrownianMassZeroFreeIntervals.lean` passes that bound along the actual selected path subsequence. The width tends to zero and the selected path coordinates converge to the continuous limit, so the limiting increment is zero on every interval with a positive lower bound on |B|. On a compact zero-free interval, continuity of the actual Brownian path gives an attained strictly positive minimum of |B|. This supplies the lower bound rather than assuming one uniformly across samples.

The result holds on one probability-one event for every pair s<=t: if B_u!=0 for all u in [s,t], then L_s=L_t. A native contrapositive theorem proves that any strict increase of L across such an interval forces a Brownian zero somewhere in that interval. The all-interval quantifier follows pathwise from the existing good convergence event, not from an uncountable intersection of fixed-interval almost-sure events.

### 473 — construct the Stieltjes measure and prove support containment

`Foundation/BrownianMassStieltjesSupport.lean` constructs a genuine samplewise Stieltjes function from the continuous limiting path when it is monotone, and uses the constant-zero Stieltjes function otherwise. The good branch occurs almost surely by469. Both branches are continuous and monotone, so their native Stieltjes measures exist; continuity proves zero mass for every singleton, including time0.

The verified interval formula is, almost surely for all s,t,

mu_omega((s,t])=ofReal(L_t(omega)-L_s(omega)).

The corresponding closed-interval formula follows from the actual left-limit continuity. Hence zero-free compact intervals have zero Stieltjes mass. Around any nonzero Brownian value, continuity supplies a closed interval neighborhood contained in the zero-free open set. Its zero mass contradicts membership in the measure support. The native theorem consequently proves

support(mu_omega) subset {t>=0:B_t(omega)=0} almost surely.

Since the nonnegative time line is hereditarily Lindelof, the measure gives zero mass outside its support; the native concentration theorem therefore proves mu_omega{t:B_t!=0}=0. This is a full support/concentration statement for the constructed Stieltjes measure, stronger than just interval constancy. The module does not yet prove that omega->mu_omega is a measurable measure-valued kernel. The underlying continuous path map is already measurable; the samplewise measure construction and its support are what is formalized here.

### 474 — rule out the trivial zero-mass construction

`Foundation/BrownianMassNontriviality.lean` uses the actual nondegenerate Gaussian law at each T>0 to prove |B_T|>0 almost surely. The sign Ito integral is centered by456. The actual coordinate identification470 and genuine integrability then give

E[L_T]=E[|B_T|]>0 for every T>0.

The native Stieltjes interval identity and L_0=0 identify the finite horizon mass with L_T almost surely. Thus E[mu_omega((0,T])]>0 for every positive T. This rules out an identically zero family. It does not claim that every sample has positive mass on every horizon, nor supply an explicit Gaussian expectation formula.

### Consequences and remaining construction boundary

The continuous Tanaka-residual path now produces actual atomless, nontrivial Stieltjes mass concentrated on the original Brownian zeros. This supplies the support property missing in470 and gives a rigorous positive counterpart to the ordinary-density obstruction454–455. A formal mutual-singularity theorem relative to the chosen nonnegative-time Lebesgue measure would still need its measure-conversion details; no such extra Lean theorem is claimed here.

The full occupation/local-time identity, the relationship between the Tanaka convention and a specified sticky speed/reference parameter, measurability/adaptedness of the random inverse and strong Markov/sticky-generator identification remain unproved. Compatible multi-point motions and genuine stochastic kernel-flow reconstruction remain further requirements. A zero-supported increasing path does not by itself prove those stochastic laws. No genuine sticky flow, NS/YM equivalence, continuum gap or Millennium result is asserted.

## Discoveries 475–476 — a measurable temporal-mass kernel and a spatial-identification obstruction

At the completed zero-support proof break, selectively revisited the sticky archive rather than reading another manuscript in full. Read the title/abstract opening and flow convention of `StickyFlowNoiseLift.tex` (title92–95, abstract99–118, flow/n-point setup375–430), and the reference-measure convention of `StickyFlowGammaSeed.tex` (300–334). The preserved source hashes are:

- `StickyFlowNoiseLift.tex`: `A4D9D6288F44A0831E7EABC05458E0F19364D1CF308B2E0305A81D8E14DC2F04`.

The noise-lift setup explicitly imports an existing jointly measurable stochastic flow and n-point generator/reference data. The seed convention lists possible diagonal reference measures and delegates the actual choice and rescaling to its LJR convention. Those source statements do not construct the objects in Lean. The new specific question is whether the constructed Brownian temporal mass now forms a measurable family, and whether its scalar Brownian observation could itself supply a spatial reference measure.

### 475 — close the measure-family measurability gap

`Foundation/BrownianMassMeasurableKernel.lean` proves that the subset of continuous paths which are monotone is closed in path space, by continuous evaluation into the pointwise function space. Its pullback through the already proved measurable path map is measurable. Thus the good/bad branch of the samplewise Stieltjes construction is measurable at each evaluation time; every cumulative coordinate is an actual measurable function of the sample.

Restricting each Stieltjes measure to [0,T] gives a genuinely finite measure for every sample, by the native interval formula. On the generating pi-system of initial intervals, evaluation of these restricted measures is an explicit measurable difference of cumulative coordinates. The finite-measure pi-system theorem proves measurability of the restricted measure-valued map.

Finally, the increasing integer-horizon restrictions exhaust every measurable time set. Continuity of measure from below expresses its full mass as a countable supremum of measurable finite-horizon evaluations. This proves actual measurability of omega->mu_omega as a map into the measurable space of measures. The module constructs a native `ProbabilityTheory.Kernel SampleSpace NNReal` whose value is exactly the previously constructed Stieltjes measure.

This is a kernel of temporal mass indexed by samples. No Markov/probability normalization, sticky transition semigroup or stochastic flow property is asserted for it. The new theorem closes the measure-valued measurability gap explicitly left at474, while retaining the earlier zero support and nontriviality results.

### 476 — the same-coordinate pushforward collapses to an atom

`Foundation/BrownianMassObservationCollapse.lean` constructs the actual finite-horizon measure obtained by pushing mu_omega restricted to [0,T] through the same continuous Brownian observation t->B_t(omega). The zero-concentration theorem474 proves that this observation equals0 almost everywhere for that temporal measure. Native pushforward congruence and the constant-map formula therefore give, almost surely for every T,

(B_omega)_*(mu_omega restricted to [0,T]) = ofReal(L_T(omega)) * delta_0.

The mass at time0 itself is zero, so this agrees with the earlier (0,T] accumulated-mass convention. The theorem is about actual measures on the real observation space, not a heuristic support comparison.

An explicit native counterexample to identifying this pushforward with spatial Lebesgue measure evaluates the interval (1,2]: the pushforward gives0, while Lebesgue measure gives1. Consequently the two measures are unequal, almost surely for every finite horizon. This rules out the naive scalar-coordinate substitution even though the temporal mass is nontrivial in expectation on positive horizons.

### What the source comparison does and does not settle

The temporal measure constructed here lives on NNReal. A deterministic diagonal reference measure in the seed manuscript lives on Delta identified with the spatial real line. These domains and roles are different. The newly verified kernel makes temporal mass integration rigorous; it does not turn the time axis into the spatial diagonal automatically.

The scalar pushforward counterexample does not refute the manuscript's unspecified intended diagonal pushforward. For a collision pair, a map involving both particle positions or their common position could retain spatial information even though the difference vanishes. Constructing that pair, specifying the map, and proving how its additive functional relates to a deterministic generator reference measure remain separate mathematical requirements. No LJR convention, endpoint parametrization or cited external theorem was independently certified by the short source reading.

This is a useful connection between the native random-measure kernel machinery, local-time support and the reference-measure audit: measurability is now proved, while a tempting spatial identification is explicitly disproved. The occupation formula, sticky parameter/speed-measure identification, measurable adapted inverse clock and strong Markov/sticky-generator law remain unproved. Compatible multi-point motions and genuine stochastic kernel-flow reconstruction remain further obligations.

## Discoveries 477–479 — an instantiated random clock and measurable Brownian time change

Returned from the selective source/reference-measure comparison475–476 to construction. The immediate question was whether the existing deterministic inverse-clock machinery424 can now be instantiated with the actual Brownian mass, including measurability of the random inverse. Rechecked the current cumulative mass/kernel interfaces, raw-past coordinate theorem and deterministic clock. No new manuscript proof or bulk intake occurred; source context remains the user's genuine sticky-flow question and the preserved sticky manuscripts already cited475–476.

### 477 — an everywhere valid measurable mass-clock input

`Foundation/BrownianRandomMassClock.lean` defines the nonnegative mass path as the positive-real conversion of cumulative(t)-cumulative(0). The samplewise cumulative function is always continuous and monotone, using its already specified zero branch off the monotonicity event. Hence the difference is nonnegative for every sample, starts at zero exactly, and is continuous and monotone. No extra random-path hypothesis is supplied to the clock constructor.

The mass coordinates and joint time/sample map are proved measurable from the verified cumulative-coordinate measurability. On one probability-one event, for every source time simultaneously, its real value equals the previously constructed Tanaka-residual path L. Centering therefore produces an everywhere valid deterministic-clock input while retaining the actual stochastic mass almost surely.

The native deterministic theorem424 is then instantiated with this mass to construct

C_kappa(omega,s)=s+kappa*mass(omega,s).

For every nonnegative kappa and every sample this forward clock is continuous, strictly increasing, onto the nonnegative line, and zero initially. Its coordinates and joint time/sample map are measurable. This closes the previously uninstantiated-clock-input gap without claiming a stochastic law for the resulting time change.

### 478 — measurable inverse and an actual continuous time-changed path

`Foundation/BrownianMassRandomTimeChange.lean` constructs the actual inverse tau_kappa(omega,t) from the instantiated order isomorphism. Native theorems give both inverse identities, continuity, monotonicity, tau(t)<=t and the deterministic increment bound tau(t)-tau(s)<=t-s.

The inverse measurability proof uses an exact order identity:

tau_kappa(omega,t)<b iff t<C_kappa(omega,b).

The right side is a measurable sample event for each b, so the initial-interval criterion proves actual measurability of every inverse coordinate. Continuity in physical time then proves joint measurability and a measurable continuous-path-valued inverse. This is a proof for the actual random inverse; its measurability is not assumed from an informal inverse selection.

The module constructs the actual continuous Brownian time change

Y_kappa(omega,t)=B(omega,tau_kappa(omega,t)),

and proves its coordinate, path-space and joint measurability using continuous evaluation. The forward clock, inverse and Brownian path all use the same Gaussian sample; no independence between the clock and Brownian path is assumed.

The exact inverse balance is tau(t)+kappa*mass(tau(t))=t. The all-source-time almost-sure agreement from477 permits substitution of the random source time, proving on one good event for all physical times

tau(t)+kappa*L_(tau(t))=t.

The native recovery identity Y(C(s))=B(s) holds for every sample. At kappa=0 the inverse is the identity and the entire changed path equals the original continuous Brownian path. These are genuine path constructions and equalities, not stochastic-generator assertions.

### 479 — the precise raw-past threshold-event result

`Foundation/BrownianMassClockPastEvents.lean` proves raw-past almost-everywhere strong measurability of mass(s) and C_kappa(s), using the independently verified fixed-time residual measurability470 and the all-time agreement477. The non-strict inverse identity is

tau_kappa(omega,t)<=s iff t<=C_kappa(omega,s).

For each fixed kappa,t,s the proof constructs an actual set A in the raw Brownian past sigma-algebra at s whose membership agrees almost surely with the inverse threshold event. This provides a verified raw measurable representative for each threshold event.

It does not prove that the actual chosen inverse threshold event itself belongs pointwise to the raw sigma-algebra, or assert Mathlib's `IsStoppingTime` for that raw filtration. A null-set augmentation/completed-filtration construction, with the necessary inclusions and retained Brownian laws proved, is a concrete remaining foundation. Almost-sure equality of sets is not silently substituted for raw pointwise measurability.

### What is now instantiated, and what remains

The clock and inverse machinery now has an actual Brownian-mass instantiation and a measurable continuous time-changed Brownian path. This advances beyond a deterministic template with an assumed local-time input. The inverse balance alone is not the physical-time occupation identity at zero. The occupation formula, the relation of kappa to a specified sticky speed/reference parameter, stopping-time/strong Markov identification and the sticky martingale problem or generator remain unproved. No Markov law or transition semigroup for Y is asserted yet.

Even a verified one-point sticky diffusion would not alone construct compatible multi-point motions or a stochastic flow of kernels. Those remain required before the existing abstract operator/semigroup machinery can be claimed to instantiate a genuine sticky stochastic flow. The earlier scalar-observation collapse476 retains its temporal-versus-spatial scope and is not bypassed by this clock construction.

## Discoveries 480–482 — null augmentation, genuine inverse stopping times and continuous martingales

### 480. A reusable augmentation inside the given ambient sigma-algebra

`Foundation/AmbientNullAugmentation.lean` constructs `augment m μ`: its events are ambient measurable sets that agree almost surely with an m-measurable event. Complement and countable-union closure are proved, as are monotonicity in m, containment in the ambient space, and inclusion of raw events when m is a sub-sigma-algebra. Every ambient measurable null set belongs to the augmentation. `filtration` applies this construction time by time, preserving the filtration and its ambient bound.

`measurable_of_raw_aestronglyMeasurable` promotes an ambient measurable, raw almost-everywhere strongly measurable map into a pseudo-metric Borel space to an actually augmented-measurable map. For a finite ambient measure and m below the ambient sigma-algebra, `condExp_invariant` proves that every real integrable function has the same conditional expectation before and after augmentation. The proof uses raw measurable representatives of augmented test events and native conditional-expectation uniqueness, not an assumed preservation law.

This is null saturation **within the original ambient measurable space**. It neither adds arbitrary non-ambient-measurable subsets of null sets nor proves full measure completion, right continuity or the usual conditions. An elaboration failure during development identified a real Lean bookkeeping hazard: the raw measurable-space parameter must precede the ambient instance so that almost-everywhere and integrability statements use the intended ambient measure. The final public types were inspected with this distinction explicit.

### 481. The actual random inverse clock is a bounded stopping time

`Foundation/BrownianMassClockStoppingTime.lean` defines `augmentedPast` from the actual Gaussian Brownian natural filtration and probability measure. The actual normalized mass and forward clock are measurable at their own times and strongly adapted. `inverse_isStoppingTime κ t` proves Mathlib's `IsStoppingTime` for the actual random inverse clock, valued in `WithTop NNReal`. Its event identity is the genuine pathwise equivalence τ(t) ≤ s iff t ≤ A(s); the raw measurable event version established in479 supplies the representative required by augmentation. Ambient measurability comes from the constructed inverse coordinate, not an assumption of adaptedness. `inverse_stopping_bounded` gives τ(t) ≤ t at every sample. `condExp_unchanged` instantiates480 for this filtration.

This closes the explicit filtration gap recorded in479 for the augmented filtration. It does not establish raw pointwise stopping-time status, nor does bounded stopping-time status alone establish optional sampling, strong Markov, transition laws or a sticky flow.

### 482. Actual continuous versions retain martingale structure

`Foundation/BrownianAugmentedMartingales.lean` proves `brownian_martingale` for the already constructed continuous Brownian path under `augmentedPast`, using coordinate almost-everywhere identification with the raw Gaussian process, raw Hermite conditional expectations of degree1 and480. Integrability and strong adaptedness of the actual continuous version are separately proved.

`signIntegralPath ω t = abs(clockPath ω t) - limitPath ω t` defines an actual continuous path at every sample. `signIntegral_coordinate_ae` identifies each fixed-time coordinate with the existing sign Itô integral. ## Discoveries 483–485 — exact clock-measure transport and nontrivial physical holding

### 483. Pushforward transport of the actual clock measure

`Foundation/BrownianClockMeasureTransport.lean` defines `ordinaryTime` on NNReal explicitly as the image of positive real Lebesgue measure under `Real.toNNReal`. This avoids silently postulating a new volume instance or replacing physical time with an arbitrary reference measure. `positive_preimage_Iic` and `ordinaryTime_Iic` identify every initial interval: its measure is exactly its endpoint.

`measure_ext_initial` is a reusable measure extensionality theorem on NNReal: finite values on initial intervals, and agreement there, imply equality of the full measures. Its proof uses the Borel-generating initial-interval pi-system and a natural-number exhaustion, so no unproved global-finiteness assumption is needed.

The actual mass Stieltjes measure satisfies `massMeasure_Iic ω t = mass ω t`, in ENNReal, at every sample, including the normalized fallback versions outside the almost-sure good set. `clockMeasure κ ω` is the genuine measure ordinaryTime + κ times massMeasure. `clockMeasure_Iic`, `forward_preimage_Iic` and `forward_map_clockMeasure` prove that its image under the actual forward clock is exactly ordinaryTime. This is a full equality of measures, not only a formal increment analogy or an assumed change-of-variables formula. Continuity, strict monotonicity and the already constructed inverse identities discharge its measurability and interval preimage obligations.

### 484. Exact occupation of zero after the random time change

`Foundation/BrownianStickyOccupation.lean` first proves `ordinaryTime_cut`, identifying restricted NNReal-time events with their real Lebesgue-time preimages. `brownian_zero_ordinary` transfers the verified original Brownian zero-occupation result to this measure; countable exhaustion yields a single good event for the entire half-line.

`zero_occupation` proves, on one probability-one event and simultaneously for every nonnegative κ and every nonnegative physical horizon T,

    ordinaryTime {t ≤ T : changedPath κ ω t = 0}
      = κ * mass ω (inverse κ ω T).

Its proof pulls the physical zero set back through the forward clock. The ordinary-time part vanishes by Brownian zero occupation; the singular mass part equals the whole mass of the inverse horizon because massMeasure is concentrated on Brownian zeros. `zero_occupation_gap` then uses the actual clock balance to identify this quantity with ENNReal.ofReal(T − inverse κ ω T). `zero_occupation_real` proves the same statement for real Lebesgue measure restricted to (0,T], applied to the genuine continuous changed path at `t.toNNReal`. The zero endpoint has no hidden contribution.

This closes the physical-time occupation obligation previously left open in482 for this constructed process and this exact clock coefficient. It does not identify the mass with an externally normalized local-time or Revuz convention, nor construct a transition law, strong Markov property or a stochastic flow.

The construction also resolves the apparent tension with454–455: original Brownian zero sets have zero ordinary time and cannot carry a nonzero ordinary-time density, yet their singular Stieltjes mass becomes positive physical occupation after the verified clock transport. The time measure changes; no absolute-continuity assumption or prohibited density shortcut has been used. The scalar spatial observation of this temporal mass still collapses to the Dirac measure at zero as shown in476; the new physical-time result does not turn it into a spatial Lebesgue diagonal measure for the manuscripts' multi-particle claims.

### 485. Holding is nontrivial at every positive deterministic horizon

`Foundation/BrownianStickyNontriviality.lean` defines `occupation` as the real value of the actual physical zero-set measure, not just as an independently specified clock gap. It is everywhere nonnegative; `occupation_gap` identifies it almost surely, simultaneously in κ and T, with T minus the actual inverse clock. `occupation_integrable` proves integrability for each parameter and horizon using that measurable bounded gap and its almost-everywhere identity.

`occupation_pos_iff` proves the useful order connection: for κ > 0, positive physical zero occupation by T is equivalent almost surely to positive constructed mass at the original Brownian time T. The strict inverse-clock threshold law, rather than independence of the clock and path, supplies this equivalence. `expected_occupation_pos` and `positive_occupation_probability` prove positive expected holding and positive probability of positive holding for every κ > 0 and every T > 0. They reuse the verified positive expectation of the constructed Brownian mass. They do not claim holding is almost surely positive at every such horizon. `occupation_parameter_zero` gives vanishing occupation for κ = 0, consistent with the recovered original Brownian path.

### Scope, remaining foundations and source provenance

The actual continuous Brownian time change now has the exact sticky-type physical occupation relation and nontrivial holding, in addition to the bounded inverse stopping-time and continuous-martingale foundations from480–482. This is a substantive realization result. A genuine sticky stochastic flow and instantiation of its transition semigroup/operator theory remain unproved: continuous-time sampling or stopped-process calculus, strong Markov/transition kernels, generator and boundary identification, matching to manuscript speed/diagonal conventions, compatible finite-particle laws and flow consistency still require independent proofs. ## Discoveries 488–490 — actual smooth strained Burgers vortex and the axial pressure boundary term

After the verified lattice checkpoint487, selectively screened existing source/report indices and returned to a distinct unresolved PDE question in `ResearchSources/Incoming/paper3_burgers_v1.tex`, SHA256 `A091CB020C8CB7838B27DD4157C98F14FCD0ACD5F61621AF39583C74B14195F1`. ### 488. Reusable smooth parameter-integral profile calculus

`Foundation/GaussianSwirlProfileMoments.lean` constructs the actual scalar moment family

    moment(n,s) = (1/2) integral from0 to1 of (-t)^n exp(-t*s) dt.

`moment_hasDerivAt` proves its derivative is moment(n+1,s), for every natural n and every real s, by local dominated differentiation under the parameter integral. On the fixed interval, abs((-t)^(n+1)) ≤1 gives a common local exponential majorant. `moment_contDiff` and `moment_smooth` prove every finite derivative order and genuine C-infinity regularity. Degree0 is the previously constructed regular swirl profile h, and degree1 its actual derivative. The constructed radial pressure is also C-infinity. Differentiating the native curl identity gives

    4 h'(s) + 2 s h''(s) = -exp(-s).

The x/y chain rules needed for actual second spatial derivatives are proved. All statements include s=0; no quotient by radius or omitted vortex-axis case appears. This supplies a reusable analytic kernel family, rather than assuming the smoothness of a singular-looking quotient formula.

### 489. A genuine smooth stationary viscous profile, including the axis

`Foundation/StrainedBurgersVortex.lean` constructs, for real nu and gamma, s=x^2+y^2,

    u = (-2 nu x - gamma y h(s), -2 nu y + gamma x h(s), 4 nu z),
    p = gamma^2 P(s) - 2 nu^2 s - 8 nu^2 z^2,

where the already constructed radial pressure satisfies P'(s)=h(s)^2/2. For positive nu this is the matched stationary Burgers-vortex family with strain rate4nu and the specified Gaussian core width. Gamma is the amplitude parameter; no unproved circulation-normalization statement is attached to it.

`velocity_smooth` and `pressure_smooth` are joint C-infinity theorems on the actual three-dimensional real coordinate space. Native `HasDerivAt` theorems for all three velocity coordinates identify every displayed Jacobian entry with an actual partial derivative. The velocity is divergence-free. Its actual coordinate Laplacian is

    (2 gamma y exp(-s), -2 gamma x exp(-s), 0).

`stationary_navier_stokes` proves the stationary momentum equation (u dot grad)u + grad p = nu Delta u at every spatial point. `vorticity_eq` proves curl u = (0,0,gamma exp(-s)). These are actual smooth functions and derivative identities, not an affine surrogate, an assumed coefficient system or a generic conditional PDE theorem. The algebraic identities allow all real parameters; the positive-viscosity interpretation uses nu>0.

The independent standard-library finite-difference probe `.lake/stardust-489-probe.py` tested the momentum residual at the axis and two off-axis points, with nu=0.3 and gamma=1.2; residuals were below6e-9. ### 490. Zero trace does not remove the strain-pressure boundary contribution

`Foundation/BurgersAxialPressureFlux.lean` defines the pressure Hessian from actual derivatives of the actual pressure gradient, and the vorticity Jacobian from actual vorticity derivatives. The diagonal pressure-Hessian entries are proved; `pressure_poisson` checks the full native compatibility trace(Hess p) = -trace((grad u)^2). `trace_square_zero` verifies the genuine source symmetry identity trace((grad omega)^2)=0. At the same time, `hessian_zz`, `contraction_eq` and `contraction_neg` prove

    omega dot (Hess p) omega = -16 nu^2 gamma^2 exp(-s)^2 <0

when nu and gamma are nonzero. The straight vortex is not pointwise pressure-neutral in this strained family. There is no contradiction with the trace identity: the axial pressure is quadratic and contributes a nonzero boundary flux.

`axial_integral_boundary` proves the exact finite-interval relation

    integral from a to b of omega dot (Hess p) omega dz
      = [omega_z^2 partial_z p] at b minus its value at a.

`unit_slab_contraction` and `trace_does_not_cancel_slab` give an explicit nonzero unit-slab pressure integral while the corresponding integral of p times trace((grad omega)^2) vanishes. These are axial interval integrals at fixed x,y. They are not silently substituted for the source's whole-space or torus integrals. `axial_unbounded_above` proves that the actual velocity is unbounded along the axis when nu is nonzero, and `axial_unit_not_periodic` proves failure of axial unit periodicity.

## Discoveries 493–495 — actual phase-dependent pressure pairing, absolute integrability and both Fubini orders

### 493. Parity and genuine Gaussian-to-volume transport

`Foundation/GaussianPlaneParity.lean` proves that the physical quarter-variance product Gaussian is preserved by simultaneous transverse negation. It proves the corresponding odd-integral identity and the zero pairing of any even plane function with x*sin(theta)-y*cos(theta). Actual pressure applications separately establish integrability; the generic Bochner odd-integral identity is not used to replace a missing domain proof.

`weighted_integrable` and `weighted_integral` transport integrable functions under the actual density (2/pi)*exp(-2(x^2+y^2)) to the ordinary plane volume integral weighted by the squared Gaussian vortex profile. `phase_integrable` uses actual Gaussian L2 pressure membership and the verified coordinate-weight estimates. Consequently the linear-trace pressure pairing is genuinely integrable and zero for every even pressure cross-section. The reusable result does not require axial independence or periodic pressure.

### 494. The actual phase-dependent base pressure has a constant transverse pairing

`Foundation/BurgersRepairedTracePairing.lean` uses the actual function P(nu,gamma,theta)(x,y), with theta in its axial pressure term, and the native Jacobian of the already constructed solenoidal repaired vorticity field. The integrand is exactly pressure times trace((grad correctedOmega)^2), not a frozen plane surrogate.

The actual pressure is even under simultaneous x,y negation. The native trace splits into epsilon times the odd linear trace plus4*epsilon^2*profile^2*R, where R=2(x^2+y^2)-1. For every theta, the first pairing vanishes by transverse parity. The quadratic pairing is the verified radial observation; the axial quadratic pressure is a constant in each cross-section and contributes zero against the centered radial weight. Every transverse integral is proved integrable.

`crossSection_exact` proves that its value is independent of theta and equals

    (pi/2)*epsilon^2*[gamma^2*log(9/8)-4*nu^2].

The axial cross-section function is interval-integrable, and its exact integral on any real oriented interval a..b is (b-a) times that value. This is an exact polynomial-in-epsilon identity for the prescribed base pressure, not an assumed asymptotic O(epsilon^2) estimate.

### 495. Absolute integrability on the product space and genuine Fubini

`Foundation/BurgersPhaseProductIntegral.lean` constructs the actual restricted axial measure volume on(a,b] and proves it finite. The raw three-variable integrand is decomposed natively into six separated plane-times-axial terms. The plane coefficients are profile-squared times pressure-weighted coordinates, coordinates alone, the radial-pressure product and the radial weight alone. Their integrability comes from493 and the actual Gaussian pressure domain. The axial factors are continuous trigonometric/polynomial functions on finite intervals.

`joint_integrable` proves absolute Bochner integrability with respect to ordinary plane volume times the restricted axial Lebesgue measure whenever a≤b. This supplies the hypotheses of native Fubini, rather than inferring joint integrability from finite iterated values. `product_integral_exact`, `period_product_exact` and `phase_first_exact` identify the genuine product integral and both integration orders. On the finite phase interval0..2pi the result is

    pi^2*epsilon^2*[gamma^2*log(9/8)-4*nu^2].

Thus the value anticipated by the frozen-z functional492 is now independently justified for the actual phase-dependent base-pressure trace integrand. No pressure periodicity is assumed merely because the integration interval has length2pi. The domain is explicitly the plane times a finite axial interval.

## Discoveries 499–500 — exact conditional-update entropy and finite boundary obstructions

At the natural proof break following498, returned to the broader archive rather than extending the Burgers calculation indefinitely. Selected `ResearchSources/Incoming/entropy_ym (4).tex`, SHA256 `09827CC13CAFF0713CBE62B049BAE3B344DFB995E85A1D0DCAC38E4370E96D03`. Read only the theorem statements around131–215 and, for the precise question below, the complete short KL-chain-rule proof at403–417. A bounded keyword index located those passages. No other full manuscript proof was ingested and no instruction in the source was acted on. The concrete question was whether an exact conditional-entropy recursion itself supplies a positive dissipation fraction for the actual finite-word SU(2) conditional-resampling kernel constructed at444–445.

### 499. A native bridge from the actual update kernel to measure-theoretic relative entropy

New module: `Foundation/ConditionalResamplingEntropy.lean`,15 public declarations. This uses Mathlib's existing measure-theoretic `InformationTheory.klDiv` and composition-product chain rule; it does not reimplement relative entropy or replace it by a formal scalar variable. Let K be a Markov kernel from a measurable boundary space P to an interior space E, and U its verified boundary-preserving conditional-resampling update. For a finite joint law J and finite boundary reference tau:

    KL(U J || tau compProd K) = KL(J.fst || tau).

For another Markov conditional L and finite boundary law pi, the exact decomposition is:

    KL(pi compProd L || tau compProd K)
      = KL(U(pi compProd L) || tau compProd K)
        + KL(pi compProd L || pi compProd K).

`entropy_decomposition_of_conditional` also gives this statement for an actual joint J supplied with its conditional kernel L. These equalities are in ENNReal, so they remain meaningful for infinite divergence and require neither illegal infinity subtraction nor finiteness of the log-likelihood integral. The additive chain rule is the genuine identity; writing W_after = W_before - D or dividing by W requires the additional finiteness and nonzero assumptions appropriate to that operation.

Every pi compProd K is stationary under U. If pi differs from tau, its entropy against tau compProd K is strictly positive, whereas its conditional entropy against pi compProd K is exactly zero. `no_positive_dissipation_fraction` proves the failure of every strictly positive multiplicative conditional-dissipation lower bound on this whole class. This is stronger than merely observing nonuniqueness of stationary laws: it identifies the exact surviving entropy as boundary information.

The obstruction is also realized by actual probability measures with finite positive entropy. Define binaryReference(a,b) = (dirac(a)+dirac(b))/2. Native proofs establish probability normalization, dirac(a) absolutely continuous with respect to that reference, distinctness for measurable distinct atoms, finite KL of the corresponding composition-products and strictly positive real KL. `binary_no_strict_contraction` disproves every real factor q<1 for this explicit pair under U. `bool_counterexample` instantiates the distinct atoms as false and true, without an assumed existence of a nontrivial boundary. These are genuine measures and an actual kernel update, not an abstract entropy recurrence.

### 500. Instantiation for the constructed SU(2) interaction and Haar-based heat bath

New module: `Foundation/SU2HeatBathEntropy.lean`,6 public declarations. `actual_joint_entropy_after_update` identifies the relative entropy of any finite joint input after the actual finite-word SU(2) heat-bath update, **against the previously constructed globally normalized interaction law**, with the entropy of its original boundary marginal against the actual interaction boundary marginal. `actual_joint_entropy_decomposition` supplies the full additive identity for an actual input composition-product pi compProd L. These use the native joint factorization, boundary probability and measurable Markov kernel; the SU(2) objects are not replaced by a convenient scalar model.

`binary_boundary_obstruction` specializes the finite positive-entropy obstruction to the same SU(2) conditional kernel for a finite boundary index space. `opposite` is the actual determinant-one unitary matrix rotation(pi) = -I, and `one_ne_opposite` proves it differs from I by inspecting a matrix entry. `concrete_haar_obstruction` uses the actual quaternionically constructed Haar law for the resampled link, the explicit boundary configurations constantly I and constantly -I on Unit, any finite collection of words, any real interaction beta, and any q<1.

Scope distinction: the concrete obstruction's reference is **the two-atom boundary probability composed with the actual Haar-based conditional kernel**. It is not identified with the original Haar-boundary globally normalized Wilson-type joint law. The first two theorems address that original joint law directly, but no finite nonzero boundary-tilt witness relative to its continuous boundary marginal is newly constructed here. ### Source assessment and next mathematical questions

The source's short chain-rule proof403–417 correctly identifies the coarse reference as the exact boundary marginal of the fine reference. ### 515. Actual time integration of the deterministic response profiles

New module: `Foundation/ExponentialResponseTimeIntegral.lean`,9 public declarations. Reuses the actual TimeHilbert=L2(Lebesgue) profile

    k_t(u)=1_(0,t](u)*exp(-lambda*(t-u)),

with lambda>0. The time parameter curve is already known to be norm-continuous. Construct a genuine jointly measurable triangular scalar kernel on(s,u), whose time slices are actual representatives of k_s. For s in(0,T], its absolute value is dominated by the fixed L2 majorant1_(0,T](u). This majorant has finite support in Lebesgue time; no constant majorant on the entire infinite Lebesgue line is assumed integrable.

The scalar column calculation is proved by ordinary FTC, with the triangular support and endpoint cases treated explicitly:

    integral_(0,T] k_s(u) ds
      = lambda^(-1)*(1_(0,T](u)-k_T(u)).

An independently supplied L2 class on the right has its actual representative proved by the Lp scalar/subtraction identities. The existing `BochnerL2Fubini.integral_eq_of_slices` theorem then identifies the actual Bochner integral, after verifying integrability, joint measurability, slice formulas and the L2 majorant:

    integral_0^T responseVector(lambda,s) ds
      = lambda^(-1)*(timeVector(T)-responseVector(lambda,T)).

The right side is not taken as the definition of the time integral. Its equality to that integral is the new proved fact. The lambda>0 hypothesis is substantive; this formula is not asserted by evaluating a totalized inverse at lambda=0.

### 516. Transport to the actual Gaussian stochastic-integral realization

New module: `Foundation/GaussianVolterraDriftBalance.lean`,14 public declarations. The actual isonormal embedding is the composition of the constructed Hilbert-coordinate embedding and the verified Gaussian first-chaos isometry. The actual exponential convolution Z_t is identified with the image of its actual response vector under this isometry. Its norm continuity, finite-interval Bochner integrability and the actual primitive

    P_T = integral_0^T Z_s ds

are established. The continuous linear isometry commutes with this actual Bochner integral, so515 yields the exact Gaussian-L2 identity

    P_T = lambda^(-1)*(B_T-Z_T),
    Z_T + lambda*P_T = B_T,

where B_T is the already constructed Brownian L2 class `GaussianTimeProcess.wienerL2 T`. This is not a new assigned driving noise. It is the actual image of the interval indicator in the existing Gaussian realization.

Define the actual drift primitive D_T=-lambda*P_T. Native FTC in Gaussian L2 proves

    D'_T = -lambda*Z_T,
    Z_T = B_T+D_T,
    Z_T-D_T = B_T.

The derivative is a Gaussian-L2 derivative, not a derivative of Brownian sample paths. Its exact squared norm is

    norm(D'_T)^2 = lambda*(1-exp(-2*lambda*T))/2.

It is strictly positive for every lambda>0,T>0. Thus the intrinsic ordinary-time term is concretely nonzero at the displayed Hilbert-space derivative level; it is not merely inferred from failure of a conditional expectation identity. The new `zero_rate_value` separately proves that the zero-rate convolution equals the actual Brownian L2 class, so the positive-rate memory term and the constant-kernel case are kept distinct.

## Discoveries 524–526 — exact shear heat flow preserves shell anisotropy

The previous turn made verified progress522–523 by discharging the entire-natural-past Markov bridge. At this proof break, returned to selective PDE exploration. Refreshed the43-file inventory and checked existing report coverage to avoid repeating the g1 transfer-sign and earlier single-cone diagnostics. Selected a previously unexamined spectral-centroid question in `ResearchSources/Incoming/ns_angular_spreading_v18 (4) (1).tex`,183960 bytes, SHA256 `AE424836A188C5E0D90E4640EA3CA74B14523101C036E60A5865EFEBFA82148F`. Title33–34 is *Phase-Conjugation Antisymmetry and Angular Spreading in the 3D Navier–Stokes Nonlinearity*. The substantive selected statements are the centroid reduction2702–2730, two-shell identity2731–2757, Chebyshev sufficient condition2764–2781, Gronwall proposition2808–2827 and spectral-separation theorem2829–2851. Read their short displayed proofs and the question-justified separation proof2853–2896. No bulk full-manuscript ingestion occurred.

The source's two-shell algebra is promising and independently checkable. The subsequent proof's Step2 divides an absolute high-shell estimate by its shell enstrophy E_H, then asserts decay of normalized angular anisotropy as the high centroid grows. The viscous-mechanism remark2898 onward interprets scalar shell damping as angular equilibration. The independent test asks what actually happens in an exact noninteracting shear solution, where the NS dynamics reduce to heat damping.

### 524 — actual smooth periodic Navier–Stokes shear solutions

New module `Foundation/SpectralShearHeatFlow.lean`, namespace `OperatorDerivativeRewrite.Foundation.SpectralShearHeatFlow`, constructs an actual finite Fourier family with arbitrary natural high frequency n. For q=exp(-nu*t), r=exp(-nu*n²*t), its literal real velocity and pressure are

    u(t,x) = (2q sin(x₁) + q sin(x₂) + r sin(n x₁), 0, 0),   p=0.

`high_realization` and `velocity_formula` identify the synthesized Fourier field with this formula. The actual ordinary time derivative and the existing actual coordinate Laplacian are identified in `time_derivative`. `advection_zero`, `incompressible` and `momentum` prove the literal NS equation with pressure0. `periodic` proves period2π in every spatial coordinate; `velocity_smooth` proves joint C∞ regularity in real time and space. The profile's Hermitian symmetry is proved. General Fourier `lap_single`, the high-mode Laplacian and the profile Laplacian provide the spectral calculations. These are actual PDE solutions, not independently prescribed modal energy curves. The PDE identities hold for all real nu,t; the manuscript comparison uses positive viscosity and nonnegative time.

### 525 — a reusable normalized-shell invariant

New module `Foundation/NormalizedShellHeat.lean`, namespace `OperatorDerivativeRewrite.Foundation.NormalizedShellHeat`, works for every finite angular index set. It defines total energy, normalized shares, excess over uniform share, and squared angular anisotropy. `share_scale` proves that every nonzero common scalar factor cancels from the normalized shares, including the totalized zero-total convention. `heat_share`, `heat_excess` and `heat_anisotropy` prove that multiplication of a shell's entire angular energy vector by exp(-2*nu*frequency*t) preserves all normalized angular quantities exactly. No claim of nonlinear transfer, approximate equal shell frequencies or angular mixing is assumed. This distinguishes decay of absolute shell energies from change of their normalized proportions.

In525 the parameter named `frequency` denotes the squared-wavenumber shell centroid κ. In524 the `decay` parameter is the wavenumber itself and is squared inside its exponential. These conventions give the same physical energy factor exp(-2*nu*κ*t).

### 526 — actual coefficient weights and the centroid ratio

New module `Foundation/ShearSpectralCentroid.lean`, namespace `OperatorDerivativeRewrite.Foundation.ShearSpectralCentroid`, computes the actual Fourier coefficients of524. `sector` is the explicit antipodal partition k₂=0 versus k₂≠0; `sector_antipodal` verifies compatibility with the real field's conjugate pairs. `profile_coeff_outside` proves that no other frequencies occur beyond ±e₁,±e₂,±n e₁. For n≥2 the named coefficient calculations distinguish the low and high modes.

`twicePairEnergy` is twice a conjugate pair's Fourier enstrophy contribution,4|k|²|coefficient(k)|². `twice_pair_identity` identifies it with2|k|² times the sum of the actual positive/negative coefficient norms for every Hermitian profile. The three actual weights are

    a=4q²,   b=q²,   c=n²r²,

proved by `low_energy`, `other_energy` and `high_energy`. The common factor2 relative to pair enstrophy does not enter normalized shares or centroid ratios. The low shell has centroid1, the high shell centroidK=n²; the first angular sector contains weights a,c and the second contains b.

`sourceRatio` is the two-sector spectral-centroid expression with totalT=a+b+c, excesses e₀=(a+c)/T-1/2 and e₁=b/T-1/2, numerator e₀(a+Kc)/T+e₁b/T and denominator[(a+b+Kc)/T](e₀²+e₁²). `sourceRatio_eq` proves its exact reduction to

    (a+b+c)(a+Kc-b) / [(a+b+Kc)(a+c-b)]

under the explicit positive/nondegenerate hypotheses used by the actual field. `centroid_gt_one` and `actual_sourceRatio_gt_one` prove that this ratio is strictly above1 for every n≥2, every real viscosity and every finite real time. In particular this holds at every positive viscosity and positive time. `initial_ratio_exact` gives57/49 at n=2,t=0. The low normalized excess is exactly3/10 and its squared anisotropy is9/50; the high angular share is exactly1 and its anisotropy is1/2 at every finite time. The corresponding native declarations are `low_normalized_excess`, `low_anisotropy_exact`, `high_normalized_share` and `high_anisotropy_exact`.

The genuine source two-shell identity is independently proved by `two_shell_identity`; its weights and cross-correlations require a positive denominator and nontrivial shell weights before a strict ratio conclusion is inferred. A separate18-case numerical probe agrees with the exact initial fraction and the reversed centroid inequality; no numerical result supplies a Lean proof.

Source classification and limits: the exact two-shell algebra is genuine. Automatic normalized angular isotropization from common within-shell viscous damping fails under the actual shear example. An absolute Gronwall estimate divided by E_H is not a uniform normalized bound unless that denominator is controlled; here E_H also decays while normalized high-shell anisotropy stays fixed. The verified ratio is the spectral centroid c_cen, not the nonlinear affine-transfer ratio c^(1): this shear has zero nonlinear advection, and no nonzero T_tot denominator or spectral steady-state hypothesis is claimed. The example is an explicit two-sector, two-shell calibration with arbitrary integer high frequency. It does not by itself refute the full existential cutoff theorem as phrased: its threshold depends on u₀ and E_H, and changing n changes u₀, while sufficiently high cutoffs of a finite spectrum may leave an empty high group. A nonvacuous uniform theorem must specify these quantifiers and denominator assumptions. An infinite smooth shear spectrum with nonempty arbitrarily high tails is a promising further test, not a completed construction here. No Navier–Stokes blow-up, global regularity, NS/YM equivalence or Millennium conclusion follows. All manuscript claims outside the precise native statements remain unverified.

### 527 — actual convergent periodic Fourier jets

New module `Foundation/GaussianFourierJets.lean`, namespace `OperatorDerivativeRewrite.Foundation.GaussianFourierJets`, has14 public declarations. For integer n and nonnegative derivative order k, define

    term_k(s,n,y) = n^k exp(-s n²) cos(n y + kπ/2),
    jet_k(s,y) = sum' over integer n of term_k(s,n,y).

`bound_summable` instantiates Mathlib's `summable_pow_mul_jacobiTheta₂_term_bound` with strip parameter0 and smoothing parameter s/π, proving actual summability of |n|^k exp(-s n²) for every s>0. `term_bound` and `term_summable` prove absolute convergence of every actual jet. This prevents use of a totalized, nonconvergent sum as a substitute for the intended series.

`term_derivative` and `jet_derivative` prove ordinary spatial differentiation from jet_k to jet_(k+1). Termwise differentiation uses a summable global derivative majorant and an actually convergent base-point series. `deriv_jet` identifies the derivative function. `jet_smooth_nat` inducts on derivative order using the derivative recurrence, and `jet_smooth` proves C∞ spatial regularity. Integer trigonometric periodicity proves `term_periodic` and `jet_periodic`, with period2π.

### 528 — parameter differentiation and the heat equation

New module `Foundation/GaussianPeriodicHeat.lean`, namespace `OperatorDerivativeRewrite.Foundation.GaussianPeriodicHeat`, has14 public declarations. `term_parameter_derivative` proves that differentiation in s also takes jet order k to k+2. `parameter_derivative` justifies this for the infinite series on the open half-line s/2<u, using a summable Gaussian majorant at s/2 and actual base-point summability. It does not differentiate an unsupported formal series.

The actual profile is H(nu,t,y)=jet_0(1+nu*t,y). `time_derivative`, `spatial_derivative` and `spatial_second_derivative` identify its actual ordinary derivatives whenever1+nu*t>0. `heat_equation` proves

    derivative_t H = nu * derivative_y derivative_y H.

`initial` identifies the fixed initial profile jet_0(1,y), independent of viscosity. `profile_smooth` gives C∞ spatial regularity, and `profile_periodic` gives period2π. `positive_parameter` instantiates the positivity requirement at every nonnegative viscosity and nonnegative time. `jet_joint_continuous` proves joint continuity of every jet at every point with s>0 using a locally uniform summable majorant; `profile_joint_continuous` transports this to the physical time parameter. No newly bundled full joint C∞ theorem is claimed, although every spatial jet is smooth and all the stated joint-continuity and ordinary-derivative identities are verified.

`Foundation/QuarticAppellDualDensity.lean` uses705 to prove that no real polynomial Q satisfies E[A_n Q]=delta(n,1) for every n when a≠0. A nonzero Q has a nonzero pairing at index3deg(Q), and that index can never equal1. Equivalently, the derivative-expectation coordinate at level1 is not represented by any polynomial under the original pairing. Thus full infinite-dimensional pairing nondegeneracy does not imply the global polynomial dual asserted by the source601–605.

A constructive global substitute is realized analytically. At every positive quartic heat time t, the actual complex Schwartz density rho_n=(-1)^n D^n K_t/n! is defined. Its product with every real polynomial is integrable, and its ordinary Lebesgue integral against P is exactly the actual Appell coefficient E_t[D^n P]/n!. Consequently integral(A_k rho_n)=delta(k,n) for all k,n. This is genuine global biorthogonality between the recursively constructed polynomial family and actual rapidly decreasing densities. It avoids division by K_t at its zeros and changes of sign.

The result provides a rigorous realization of coordinate dual functionals in a larger analytic space, not a polynomial dual, an orthogonal positive chaos, or an infinite-series convergence theorem. No signed path measure or continuous-time stochastic integral is introduced. The new full-polynomial nondegeneracy also makes the previously open polynomial-probe-only Stein uniqueness question directly testable in the quartic case.

Consequently f times (−fprime/f)=−fprime almost everywhere, with the totalized quotient taking value0 at denominator0.

for every real t and natural n. The proof unfolds the existing exponential/gamma density and uses the native with-density Bochner integral theorem. For t>=0 it identifies the density-weighted integrand pointwise with the [0,t] indicator times exp(-t)(t-s)^n/n!, then evaluates the actual interval integral by a verified substitution and the power antiderivative. For t<0 the density-weighted integrand is identically zero. No integrability is assumed to obtain a desired numerical integral; the bounded cylinder construction904 supplies the genuine stochastic integrability used in the probability calculation. No gamma convolution law or new stochastic axiom is introduced.

`HigherHeatDyadicPositionRefinement` proves exact equality of any position cylinder with its corresponding endpoint cylinder on every finer grid, using the actual conditional terminal identity and native projection/refinement formulas.
